speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you describe the appearance of the rash on your trunk and extremities, specifically noting if it is red, raised, or blistered? I also need to know if you have noticed any swelling in your joints or lymph nodes.

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the facial rash involve the cheeks in a "slapped cheek" appearance, and has the trunk rash evolved into a lacy, net-like pattern? I also need to know if she has any joint pain or swelling.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of a facial rash sparing the perioral area followed by a lacy, reticular rash on the trunk and extremities is highly characteristic of Erythema Infectiosum, also known as Fifth Disease. DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
